newsitem.title: USA: Plains feedlot cattle markets slow at $72-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: Plains feedlot cattle markets slow at $72-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets were slow Thursday, with the bulk of this week's showlists sold on Wednesday, feedlot sources said.
About 5,000 head traded in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area at $72.00 per cwt, steady with Wednesday's trade. The week to date figure was pegged near 87,000 head, according to USDA.
An estimated 2,000 head traded in Kansas, also at $72.00, which brought the weekly figure close to 75,000, USDA said.
Wednesday's sales were about two to three weeks ahead of schedule and should be delivered by Wednesday, they said.
Prices the past 2-1/2 weeks have been supported by light feedlot supplies and the pulling forward of cattle marketings to meet packer demand, market sources said.
Trade Friday and early next week was seen light because of the Veterans Day holiday on Monday, with several packing plants closed, including three of 11 IBP plants in the U.S.
IBP officials said the cattle plants at Amarillo, Tex.; Emporia, Kan.; and Westpoint, Neb. would be closed Monday for the holiday and would reopen on Tuesday.
Other major meatpacking company officials had not yet announced holiday plans.
